extracted.intended_audience: registered apprenticeship program sponsors, State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), intermediaries, educators, employers, and public commenters on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and quality standards for establishing, registering, operating, reviewing, and governing registered apprenticeship programs (including CTE apprenticeships) and State Apprenticeship Agency recognition under the National Apprenticeship System. Includes procedural rules, data/reporting obligations, and enforcement processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worker protections and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Create more safeguards for apprentices to ensure that they have healthy and safe working and learning environments as well as just and equitable opportunities throughout their participation in a registered apprenticeship program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on mitigating barriers for populations historically underserved (e.g., women and people of color) and enhancing opportunities for younger workers; institutionalize DEIA as central to program oversight and access; proposed §29.2 defines 'underserved communities.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor standards attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: All apprenticeship programs must maintain labor standards that are objective, accountable, flexible and efficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department proposes modernizing and standardizing minimum labor standards combining competency- and time-based approaches into a unitary, coherent training model across all programs to support expansion into new industries and ensure industry-driven integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid training model / end-point assessment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernize training model by combining key attributes of competency- and time-based approaches and require assessment of apprentice progress by means of an end-point assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End-point assessments and certificate of program completion are proposed to help ensure apprentices obtain requisite skills and competencies for proficiency in an occupation suitable for registered apprenticeship (see §§29.13–29.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupations suitable for registered apprenticeship (Section 29.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective, proactive, and transparent process for the determination of occupations suitable for registered apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process balances flexibility for new/emerging industries with safeguards against adverse impacts to existing programs (preventing 'splintering'); includes DOL-OA occupation determination evaluation process, wage analysis and career development profile, and new requirements for on-the-job training documentation (§29.7(a)–(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of Apprenticeship (Section 29.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum required elements and quality labor standards for registered apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes requirements such as progressive wage increases, documentation of on-the-job and related instruction, and other elements to ensure apprentices' progression and welfare (references to §29.8(a)(17)(B), §29.8(a)(18), and documentation changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship Agreements (Section 29.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required content and limitations of apprenticeship agreements between apprentices and sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes to prohibit non-disclosure and non-compete provisions in apprenticeship agreements (§29.9(d)(1) and (2), (e)); details on reporting, terms of apprenticeship, wages, and protections for apprentices are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Registration (Section 29.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and process for registering an apprenticeship program with a Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers application contents, documentation, review and acceptance criteria for registration, and obligations of registered programs once approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Standards Adoption Agreement (Section 29.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Framework for sponsors to adopt and report use of National Program Standards or other standards via an adoption agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes reporting obligations for Program Standards Adoption Agreements and how adopters interact with National Program Standards and Registration Agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of Apprentice Trainers and Related Instruction Providers (Section 29.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for who may serve as apprentice trainers and providers of related classroom instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies qualification criteria, oversight, and expectations for trainers and related instruction providers to ensure quality of training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship (Section 29.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation and use of National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship to standardize occupational competencies across programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns with National Program Standards and National Guidelines to institutionalize industry-validated occupational standards to support portability and clarity of skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Program Standards for Apprenticeship (Section 29.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishment of minimum National Program Standards for registered apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to provide baseline, industry-informed program elements for quality and consistency across the National Apprenticeship System.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards (Section 29.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines to support development and interpretation of apprenticeship standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve as interpretive and implementation guidance to Registration Agencies, sponsors, and SAAs for applying program standards and occupational standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-Point Assessment and Certificate of Program Completion (Section 29.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for assessment at program completion and issuance of a certificate of completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End-point assessments validate proficiency and support awarding a nationally recognized certificate; part of proposed quality assurance for ensuring career readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints process for registered programs (Section 29.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanism for filing and handling complaints related to registered apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers submission, processing, potential remedies, and how complaints inform enforcement or program review actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping by Registered Programs (Section 29.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations for recordkeeping by program sponsors and registration agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what records must be maintained (including OJT and related instruction documentation), retention periods, and availability for review to ensure accountability and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Reviews (Section 29.19 & Part 30.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular program review procedures and standards used by Registration Agencies and OA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program reviews evaluate compliance with labor standards, training quality, data/reporting accuracy, and EEO requirements; findings may lead to corrective actions or deregistration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deregistration of a Registered Program (Section 29.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds and procedures for deregistration of apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes criteria for deregistration, notice, opportunity for hearing, and potential consequences for failing to meet standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings on Deregistration (Section 29.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules for administrative hearings related to proposed deregistration actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets forth hearing rights, evidence, decision processes, and timelines for sponsors facing deregistration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of Program Registration (Section 29.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Process and criteria for reinstating a previously deregistered apprenticeship program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes steps sponsors must take to cure deficiencies and demonstrate compliance before registration is restored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions (Section 29.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which exemptions to certain regulatory requirements may be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies who may request exemptions, applicable criteria, and any limits or reporting tied to exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of Career and Technical Education (CTE) Apprenticeship Programs (Section 29.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and processes specific to registering CTE apprenticeship programs aligned with secondary/postsecondary State-approved CTE programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes required coordination with education entities, approval of Industry Skills Frameworks (§29.24(b)), specific standards (§29.24(c)), sponsor definitions and registration (§29.24(d) and subsections), CTE apprenticeship agreements (§29.24(e)), certificates upon completion (§29.24(f)), administrative requirements (§29.24(g)), selection of diverse and inclusive cross-section of students (§29.24(d)(2)(v)(A)), sponsor oversight of participating employers, and technical assistance expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of Data and Quality Metrics Concerning Apprenticeship (Section 29.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Framework and obligations for collecting, maintaining, and reporting program- and system-level data and quality metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data used for oversight, program reviews, improved demographic tracking, and establishing performance indicators; includes references to RAPIDS and promoting State and sponsor participation in national data systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and Responsibilities of State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs) (Section 29.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Delineation of SAA duties, governance expectations, and operational responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers reciprocity, program registration processing, data reporting, and coordination with OA; includes SAA planning and accountability obligations and potential consequences for non-participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and Reporting Requirements for State Apprenticeship Agencies (Sections 29.27–29.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for OA recognition of an SAA and the reporting obligations for recognized SAAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes standards for submission of a State apprenticeship plan for recognition, ongoing reporting to demonstrate meeting governance and performance expectations, and obligations to participate in data systems and program oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of a State Apprenticeship Plan / Derecognition (Section 29.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and standards for denying SAA recognition or derecognizing existing SAAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies grounds for denial/derecognition, notice and appeal processes, and implications for state-level program operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship Requirements in Other Laws (Section 29.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interplay between registered apprenticeship regulations and other federal statutes and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies how apprenticeship obligations intersect with laws such as WIOA, Perkins, and other federal requirements; States must address program-specific requirements in unified/combined state plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 30 Revisions – EEO in Apprenticeship (Definitions, Program Reviews, Complaints, Enforcement) (Parts 30.2, 30.13–30.15, 30.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions to 29 CFR part 30 governing equal employment opportunity in apprenticeship programs, including definitions, program review processes, complaint handling, and enforcement actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical and conforming changes intended to align EEO oversight with proposed Part 29 changes; includes process for enforcement actions and severability provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State planning requirement and governance expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that States seeking SAA recognition develop a strategic vision and goals to expand and diversify registered apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must implement robust data collection/reporting to track achievement of systemwide goals; OA proposes revising governance process to promote uniformity, accountability, and innovation at State level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing, SAA reciprocity, and program registration reciprocity
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for data sharing among Registration Agencies, SAAs, and OA and rules for reciprocity of registrations across SAAs (§29.26(d), §29.28).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes obligations for submission of unified data, potential requirements to participate in RAPIDS, and mechanisms for reciprocal recognition of program registrations between SAAs and OA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage analysis and career development profile requirements (within §29.7 subject analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: New or expanded requirements to conduct wage analyses and develop career development profiles for occupations considered suitable for apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate economic mobility potential and safeguard against adverse wage impacts when approving new occupations; included in subject-by-subject economic analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-the-job training (OJT) documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: New requirements for documenting on-the-job training, including updates to OJT documentation protocols for registered programs (§29.7(b)(3) and related references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects program administrative burden and recordkeeping; considered in cost analyses and program review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on non-disclosure and non-compete provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed prohibition of non-disclosure and non-compete provisions in apprenticeship agreements (§29.9(d)(1) and (2), (e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as a benefit in the NPRM analysis; aimed at protecting apprentice mobility and economic opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of diverse and inclusive cross-section of students (CTE sponsors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement for CTE apprenticeship sponsors to select a diverse and inclusive cross-section of students when applicable (§29.24(d)(2)(v)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of CTE sponsor registration and oversight obligations intended to promote equity and broaden participation among secondary and postsecondary students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor oversight of participating employers (CTE and general sponsors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors are responsible for oversight of participating employers in apprenticeship programs, including CTE apprenticeships (§29.24(d)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes ensuring compliance with program standards, safety, wage progression, quality of OJT and related instruction, and other sponsor responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and information-collection (Paperwork Reduction Act) obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments and submissions related to information collection aspects and PRA compliance; obligations for sponsors and SAAs to report data as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department invites comment on PRA-related items and provides OIRA contact for ICR comments; data collection requirements form part of compliance burden analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired focus of public comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics the Department requests commenters focus on when submitting written comments to the NPRM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated topics: (1) Labor Standards and Equal Employment Opportunity for Registered Apprenticeship Programs—Registration and Reporting Requirements; (2) Occupational Suitability and National Occupational Standards; (3) State Apprenticeship Agency Governance and Planning; (4) Registered Career and Technical Education Apprenticeship. Comments due by March 18, 2024.
